subproblems.title: Flat decomposition of weakly convergent integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^P (Simon 6.7.1–7.2, 'only if' part)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with n := m + 1 < P. Let T_j (j ∈ ℕ) and T be integer multiplicity currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n with IsIntegerMultiplicity) such that sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and T_j ⇀ T in ℝ^P (WeaklyConvergesOn: T_j(ω) → T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)). Then for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P there are integer multiplicity currents R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (j ∈ ℕ) with T − T_j − S_j = ∂R_j for every j (Simon: T − T_j = ∂R_j + S_j) and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) → 0. Here M_W is the SimonGMT mass massOn W (Euclidean coefficient norm).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), m + 1 < P → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Bornology.IsBounded W → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + (Ts j).boundary.massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Bornology.IsBounded W → ∃ (R : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (R j) ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity (S j) ∧ T - Ts j - S j = (R j).boundary) ∧ Tendsto (fun j => (R j).massOn W + (S j).massOn W) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 7.1 and the proof of the "only if" part of Theorem 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2004–2120, printed pp. 170–172). Here U = ℝ^P, so "W ⊂⊂ U" means "W bounded", and the ambient dimension is n + ℓ = P with ℓ = P − n ≥ 1, the range n, ℓ ∈ {1, 2, …} of Simon §5. This is the result cited as (C1) in step 4 of the parent proof. The printed proof is copied. The details it leaves to the reader are written out in steps 3, 6 and 7: the localisation to a ball, the identification of the limit after localisation, and the passage from d_W(T_j, T) → 0 to explicit decompositions. In steps 4–6 the error currents S only need small mass; they need not be integer multiplicity. Integer multiplicity of the final error current is recovered in step 7 by applying boundary rectifiability to the (n+1)-current R^{(q)}. So every citation stays inside Simon's range (dimensions ≥ 1, codimension ℓ ≥ 1), also when m = 0.

Cited results of the source text, each used in its stated range:
(D) Simon 6.5.3, Deformation Theorem, scaled version (lines 1462–1480), for n-currents in ℝ^{n+ℓ}, n, ℓ ≥ 1. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with M(T) + M(∂T) < ∞ and let σ > 0. Then T − P = ∂R + S, where:
 • P = Σ_F β_F[[F]], the sum over the n-faces F of the cubical grid of side σ;
 • M(P) ≤ cM(T), M(R) ≤ cσM(T) and M(S) ≤ cσM(∂T), with c = c(n, ℓ);
 • spt P ∪ spt R ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt T) < 2√P σ} and spt S ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt ∂T) < 2√P σ}.
 If T is integer multiplicity, then P and R are integer multiplicity (β_F ∈ ℤ). Only these properties are used; S is just a current.
(BR) Simon 6.6.3, Boundary Rectifiability Theorem (lines 1993–1996). If T ∈ 𝒟_k(U) is integer multiplicity and M_V(∂T) < ∞ for all V ⊂⊂ U, then ∂T is integer multiplicity. It is used only for k = n + 1 ≥ 2.
(SL) Simon 6.4.6–4.10 (lines 1305–1385). Suppose M_V(T) + M_V(∂T) < ∞ for all V ⊂⊂ U and f is Lipschitz, and set ⟨T, f, t−⟩ := ∂(T⌞{f < t}) − (∂T)⌞{f < t}. Here T⌞E is the restriction of T to the Borel set E, defined through the measure representation of T (2.7).
 • (4.8) ⟨T, f, t−⟩ vanishes on every form whose support is disjoint from f⁻¹(t).
 • (4.9) For bounded open W: M_W(⟨T, f, t−⟩) ≤ ess sup_W|Df|·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ M_W(T⌞{t − h < f < t}).
 • The lower Dini derivative D(t) := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ_T(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) of the nondecreasing function t ↦ μ_T(W ∩ {f < t}) is measurable, with ∫_a^b D dt ≤ μ_T(W ∩ {a < f < b}). This is Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions, which is how 4.10 is derived.
(ML) Elementary mass localisation. Let X be a current that vanishes on every form whose support is disjoint from a compact set C, and let V ⊇ C be open. Then M(X) ≤ M_V(X). Proof: choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of C. For every admissible ω, tsupport((1 − χ)ω) is disjoint from C and χω is admissible for M_V, so X(ω) = X(χω) + X((1 − χ)ω) = X(χω) ≤ M_V(X).
(CO) Simon 6.3.13 (lines 905–960). Integer multiplicity currents are complete for the seminorms M_V, V ⊂⊂ U. In particular, an M-absolutely convergent series of integer multiplicity currents with supports in a fixed compact set converges in mass to an integer multiplicity current.
(R) Integer combinations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity (Simon 6.3.2(1); sibling im_calculus (c)). The restriction (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) of a representation to a Borel set E represents an integer multiplicity current (sibling im_calculus (b)).
(MM) M_V(A) = μ_A(V) for integer multiplicity A and open V (sibling mass_eq_measure), and μ_A is finite on compact sets.
(LSC) Lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (Simon 6.2.14; SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf).

Throughout, n := m + 1, ℓ := P − n ≥ 1, B_r := ball(0, r), and "IM" means integer multiplicity. For currents A, B in one domain and any V: M_V(0 − A) = M_V(A), since ω ↦ −ω preserves admissible forms, and M_V(A ± B) ≤ M_V(A) + M_V(B).

1. (The class I and the pseudometrics.) Let I be the set of IM currents A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with M_V(∂A) < ∞ for every bounded open V.
 (a) Each T_j ∈ I by hypothesis.
 (b) T ∈ I: ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T, because ∂T_j(ω) = T_j(dω) → T(dω). So by (LSC), M_V(∂T) ≤ liminf_j M_V(∂T_j) ≤ sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)) < ∞.
 (c) For A₁, A₂ ∈ I and bounded open V put (Simon 7.1) d_V(A₁, A₂) := inf{M_V(S) + M_V(R) : A₁ − A₂ = ∂R + S, with R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) IM}. The set is nonempty: R = 0 and S = A₁ − A₂, which is IM by (R).

2. (Reduction.) Fix a bounded open W. It suffices to show d_W(T_j, T) → 0.
 (a) Suppose d_W(T_j, T) → 0. For each j choose IM R'_j, S'_j with T_j − T = ∂R'_j + S'_j and M_W(R'_j) + M_W(S'_j) ≤ d_W(T_j, T) + 2^{−j}. Put R_j := 0 − R'_j and S_j := 0 − S'_j, which are IM by (R).
 (b) Then T − T_j − S_j = −(T_j − T) + S'_j = −∂R'_j = ∂R_j, and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) = M_W(R'_j) + M_W(S'_j) → 0.
 (c) Since (d_W(T_j, T))_j is a sequence in [0, ∞], it tends to 0 as soon as every subsequence has a further subsequence along which it tends to 0. This is Simon's last paragraph: "since we can thus extract a subsequence converging relative to d_W̃ from any given subsequence …". So fix an arbitrary subsequence; we keep calling it (T_j) and pass to further subsequences below.

3. (Localisation.) Simon: "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2 we can find a subsequence … with sup_j' M(∂(T_j'⌞W_i)) < ∞ … thus we can assume … spt T_j ⊆ W̄".
 (a) Choose r₀ ≥ 1 with W ⊆ B_{r₀} and let f(x) := |x|, a 1-Lipschitz function. Put V := B_{r₀+2} and Λ := sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)) < ∞.
 (b) Fix j and t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1). By 4.8 the slice ⟨T_j, f, t−⟩ vanishes on forms whose support misses the compact set f⁻¹(t) = ∂B_t ⊆ V, so M(⟨T_j, f, t−⟩) ≤ M_V(⟨T_j, f, t−⟩) by (ML). By 4.9 with W = V and |Df| ≤ 1, this is at most liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ M_V(T_j⌞{t − h < f < t}). Since {t − h < f < t} ⊆ V for 0 < h < t, the restriction T_j⌞{t − h < f < t} is IM by (R) with weight μ_{T_j}⌞{t − h < f < t}, and by (MM) its mass in V is μ_{T_j}({t − h < f < t}). Hence M(⟨T_j, f, t−⟩) ≤ D_j(t) := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ_{T_j}(V ∩ {t − h < f < t}). D_j is measurable, and ∫_{r₀}^{r₀+1} D_j dt ≤ μ_{T_j}(V) = M_V(T_j) ≤ Λ by (MM).
 (c) By Fatou's lemma, ∫_{r₀}^{r₀+1} liminf_j D_j dt ≤ Λ. So there is t₀ ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) with liminf_j D_j(t₀) < ∞. Pass to a subsequence along which Λ' := sup_j M(⟨T_j, f, t₀−⟩) < ∞.
 (d) Put W₁ := B_{t₀} and T'_j := T_j⌞W₁. T'_j is IM by (R), being represented by (M_j ∩ W₁, θ_j, ξ_j). Moreover spt T'_j ⊆ closure(W₁) and ∂T'_j = (∂T_j)⌞W₁ + ⟨T_j, f, t₀−⟩. By (MM) with V = ℝ^P, M(T'_j) = μ_{T_j}(W₁) ≤ M_V(T_j). Also M((∂T_j)⌞W₁) ≤ μ_{∂T_j}(W₁) ≤ M_V(∂T_j), where μ_{∂T_j} is the Radon measure representing ∂T_j (2.7). Hence M(T'_j) + M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ + Λ' =: M₀ for all j.
 (e) T'_j(ω) = T_j(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W₁.
 (f) closure(W) ⊆ closedBall(0, r₀) ⊆ W₁.
 Let 𝒞 be the set of IM A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt A ⊆ closure(W₁) and M(A) + M(∂A) ≤ M₀. All T'_j lie in 𝒞.

4. (Total boundedness; Simon (1)–(3).) Let W̃ := B_{t₀+1}.
 Claim: for every ε > 0 there are finitely many IM currents P₁, …, P_N ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that every A ∈ 𝒞 admits some k ≤ N, an IM R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with A − P_k = ∂R + S, spt R ∪ spt S ⊆ W̃ and M(R) + M(S) < ε.
 (a) Choose σ ∈ (0, 1) with 2√P σ < 1 and cσM₀ < ε.
 (b) Let A ∈ 𝒞. A is IM with M(A) + M(∂A) ≤ M₀ < ∞, so (D) gives IM P, R and a current S with A − P = ∂R + S and M(R) + M(S) ≤ cσ(M(A) + M(∂A)) < ε. The supports of P, R and S lie within 2√P σ of spt A ∪ spt ∂A ⊆ closure(W₁), hence in W̃.
 (c) P = Σ_F β_F[[F]] with β_F ∈ ℤ and M(P) = Σ_F |β_F|σⁿ ≤ cM₀. Since spt P ⊆ W̃, only the finitely many n-faces F of the σ-grid meeting the bounded set W̃ occur, and |β_F| ≤ cM₀σ^{−n}.
 (d) So P belongs to a finite set {P₁, …, P_N} that depends only on ε, M₀, W₁, n and ℓ.

5. (A Cauchy subsequence; Simon (5).)
 (a) Apply step 4 with ε = 2^{−r−2} for r = 1, 2, …. By the pigeonhole principle and a diagonal argument there are indices j₁ < j₂ < … and, for each r, a single P^{(r)} among the finitely many currents of step 4 (for ε = 2^{−r−2}) such that T'_{j_s} − P^{(r)} = ∂R_{s,r} + S_{s,r} for all s ≥ r. Here R_{s,r} is IM, S_{s,r} is a current, both are supported in W̃, and M(R_{s,r}) + M(S_{s,r}) < 2^{−r−2}.
 (b) Subtract the decompositions for s = r + 1 and s = r: T'_{j_{r+1}} − T'_{j_r} = ∂R_r + S_r, where R_r := R_{r+1,r} − R_{r,r} is IM by (R) and S_r := S_{r+1,r} − S_{r,r}. Both are supported in closure(W̃), and M(R_r) + M(S_r) < 2^{−r−1}.

6. (Series; Simon: "by 3.13 we can define integer multiplicity R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} by the M-absolutely convergent series".)
 (a) For q ≥ 1 the series R^{(q)} := Σ_{r ≥ q} R_r converges absolutely in mass; by (CO) its limit is IM and the partial sums converge to it in mass, hence weakly.
 (b) For each ω, Σ_{r≥q} |S_r(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·Σ_r M(S_r) < ∞. So S^{(q)}(ω) := Σ_{r ≥ q} S_r(ω) is a linear functional with |S^{(q)}(ω)| ≤ 2^{−q} sup|ω|, hence a current; it is the mass limit of the partial sums.
 (c) M(R^{(q)}) + M(S^{(q)}) ≤ Σ_{r≥q} 2^{−r−1} = 2^{−q}.
 (d) Summing step 5 for r = q, …, L − 1 gives T'_{j_L} − T'_{j_q} = ∂(Σ_{r=q}^{L−1} R_r) + Σ_{r=q}^{L−1} S_r.
 (e) Evaluate at ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W₁ and let L → ∞. We have T'_{j_L}(ω) = T_{j_L}(ω) → T(ω), (Σ_{r=q}^{L−1} R_r)(dω) → R^{(q)}(dω) and (Σ_{r=q}^{L−1} S_r)(ω) → S^{(q)}(ω). Hence
 (★) T(ω) − T_{j_q}(ω) = ∂R^{(q)}(ω) + S^{(q)}(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W₁.

7. (A global integer multiplicity decomposition.)
 (a) ∂R^{(q)} is IM. By 6(d), ∂(Σ_{r=q}^{L−1} R_r) = T'_{j_L} − T'_{j_q} − Σ_{r=q}^{L−1} S_r has mass ≤ 2M₀ + 1, and it converges weakly to ∂R^{(q)} as L → ∞. By (LSC), M(∂R^{(q)}) ≤ 2M₀ + 1 < ∞. Since R^{(q)} is an IM (n+1)-current, (BR) applies.
 (b) Put S^♯_q := (T − T_{j_q}) − ∂R^{(q)}, which is IM by (R). Then T − T_{j_q} = ∂R^{(q)} + S^♯_q.
 (c) By (★), S^♯_q(ω) = S^{(q)}(ω) for every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W₁ ⊇ W. So M_W(S^♯_q) = M_W(S^{(q)}) ≤ M(S^{(q)}).
 (d) Changing signs (R ↦ 0 − R^{(q)}, S ↦ 0 − S^♯_q) gives an IM decomposition of T_{j_q} − T. Hence d_W(T_{j_q}, T) ≤ M_W(R^{(q)}) + M_W(S^♯_q) ≤ 2^{−q} → 0 as q → ∞.

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–7, every subsequence of (T_j) has a further subsequence along which d_W(T_j, T) → 0. Hence d_W(T_j, T) → 0, and step 2 produces the required IM R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P), S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with T − T_j − S_j = ∂R_j and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) → 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: C and the T_j lie in Simon's class I (M_V(∂T) < ∞ by lower semicontinuity). It suffices to prove d_W(T_j, T) → 0 for the pseudometric of 7.1, and for that it suffices that every subsequence has a further subsequence along which it holds.
Localise: the slicing bound 4.9 (with its integrated form 4.10) and Fatou give t₀ ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) and a subsequence with M(T_j⌞B_{t₀}) + M(∂(T_j⌞B_{t₀})) ≤ M₀.

Total boundedness: the deformation theorem 5.3 writes each such current as one of finitely many integer polyhedral currents plus ∂R + S, with R integer multiplicity, supports in B_{t₀+1} and M(R) + M(S) < ε.

Pigeonhole gives T'_{j_{r+1}} − T'_{j_r} = ∂R_r + S_r with masses < 2^{−r−1}. R^{(q)} = Σ_{r≥q} R_r is integer multiplicity by 3.13, S^{(q)} = Σ_{r≥q} S_r is a current, and T − T_{j_q} = ∂R^{(q)} + S^{(q)} on forms supported in B_{t₀}.

Globalise: ∂R^{(q)} is integer multiplicity by 6.3 for the (n+1)-current R^{(q)}, so S^♯_q := T − T_{j_q} − ∂R^{(q)} is integer multiplicity and d_W(T_{j_q}, T) ≤ 2^{−q}. Conclude d_W(T_j, T) → 0 and pick near-optimal decompositions with signs changed.

subproblems.title: Slicing an integer multiplicity current with integer multiplicity boundary by a Lipschitz function (Simon 6.4.1–4.5, 4.8)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P. Let T ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R_T = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep univ (m + 2), R_T.Represents T), and let ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R_∂ = (M', θ', ξ') (IMRep univ (m + 1)). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be Lipschitz with constant L ∈ [0, ∞) (LipschitzWith L f). Then there are currents P_t ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) such that: (1) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P the function t ↦ M_W(P_t) ∈ [0, ∞] is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure and ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T); (2) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ: P_t is integer multiplicity; P_t(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) whose topological support is disjoint from f⁻¹(t); and P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{m+2} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{m+1} for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) (Hᵏ = μHE[k]). The last identity says P_t = ∂(T⌞{f < t}) − (∂T)⌞{f < t}, Simon's formula 4.5(2) for the slice ⟨T, f, t⟩.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4, Lemma 4.5 and 4.8 (chapter-06.txt lines 1151–1360, printed pp. 153–158). They are applied to the integer multiplicity (m+2)-current T = τ(M, θ, ξ) in U = ℝ^P; Simon's n is m + 2 here and the slices are (m+1)-currents. This is the result cited as (C2) in step 5 of the parent proof. The printed proofs are copied. Two points the source leaves implicit are made explicit: the family P_t is defined for every t, by the right side of 4.5(2) (step 1), and t ↦ M_W(P_t) is measurable (step 6). The hypothesis m + 1 < P only ensures that the currents considered are not trivially zero; it is not otherwise used.

Notation.
 • N := m + 2 and Hᵏ := μHE[k].
 • For x ∈ M, ∇^M f(x) is the gradient of f along M (Simon Ch. 3, 2.1). It is defined Hᴺ-a.e. on M through a decomposition M = ⋃_j M_j with Hᴺ(M₀) = 0 and M_j ⊆ N_j, N_j embedded C¹ submanifolds, and |∇^M f| ≤ L Hᴺ-a.e. on M.
 • M₊ := {x ∈ M : ∇^M f(x) ≠ 0}, and M_t := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t) for t ∈ ℝ.
 Borel versions of ∇^M f and of M₊ are fixed; this changes nothing up to Hᴺ-null sets.

1. (The currents P_t.) For every t, E_t := {f < t} is open, since f is continuous.
 (a) By the sibling im_calculus (b) (restriction of a representation to a Borel set, U = ℝ^P) there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_N(ℝ^P) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_{N−1}(ℝ^P) represented by (M ∩ E_t, θ, ξ) and (M' ∩ E_t, θ', ξ'). These are Simon's T⌞{f < t} and (∂T)⌞{f < t}.
 (b) Put P_t := ∂A_t − B_t. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^{N−1}(ℝ^P), P_t(ω) = A_t(dω) − B_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dHᴺ − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{N−1}. This is the identity in (2), and it holds for every t.

2. (Lemma 4.1: coarea on M.) For L¹-a.e. t the following hold.
 (a) M_t is countably (N−1)-rectifiable (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 2.10(2)).
 (b) For H^{N−1}-a.e. x ∈ M_t, the approximate tangent spaces T_xM_t and T_xM exist, T_xM_t is an (N−1)-dimensional subspace of T_xM, and T_xM = {y + λ∇^M f(x) : y ∈ T_xM_t, λ ∈ ℝ}. This follows from Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 applied to M_t and to M, together with ∇^M f(x) ∈ T_xM and ⟨∇^M f(x), τ⟩ = 0 for τ ∈ T_xM_t (Ch. 3, 2.1).
 (c) For every non-negative Hᴺ-measurable g on M, ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} g dH^{N−1} dt = ∫_M |∇^M f| g dHᴺ, and t ↦ ∫_{M_t} g dH^{N−1} is L¹-measurable. This is the co-area formula, Simon Ch. 3, 2.8–2.9 with m = 1.
 Replacing g by g·1_{f<t} gives Remark 4.2: t ↦ ∫_{M∩{f<t}} |∇^M f| g dHᴺ = ∫_{−∞}^t ∫_{M_s} g dH^{N−1} ds is absolutely continuous, with derivative ∫_{M_t} g dH^{N−1} for a.e. t.

3. (4.3–4.4: the slice as an integer multiplicity current.) Take t as in step 2.
 (a) For H^{N−1}-a.e. x ∈ M_t, ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ⌞ (∇^M f(x)/|∇^M f(x)|) (with ⟨ξ⌞w, a⟩ := ⟨ξ, w ∧ a⟩) is a unit simple (N−1)-vector orienting T_xM_t. Indeed (4.3), ξ(x) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_N with τ₁ = ∇^M f/|∇^M f| and τ₂, …, τ_N an orthonormal basis of T_xM_t.
 (b) Let θ_t := θ|M_t. By step 2(c) with g = θ1_K, ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t∩K} θ dH^{N−1} dt ≤ L∫_{M∩K} θ dHᴺ < ∞ for each compact K. Applying this to K = closedBall(0, k), k ∈ ℕ, θ_t is locally H^{N−1}-integrable on M_t for a.e. t.
 (c) Fix a Borel version ξ̃ of ξ; ξ is Hᴺ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. Let Z ⊆ M be an Hᴺ-null Borel set containing the points where ξ̃ ≠ ξ, where ξ does not orient T_xM, or where ∇^M f or T_xM does not exist. By step 2(c) with g = 1_Z, ∫_ℝ H^{N−1}(Z ∩ M_t) dt = ∫_Z |∇^M f| dHᴺ = 0, so H^{N−1}(Z ∩ M_t) = 0 for a.e. t. Hence for a.e. t, (a) holds at H^{N−1}-a.e. x ∈ M_t, and ξ_t agrees H^{N−1}-a.e. on M_t with the Borel field ξ̃ ⌞ (∇^M f/|∇^M f|).
 (d) Hence for a.e. t, (M_t, θ_t, ξ_t) is an integer multiplicity triple (an IMRep univ (N−1)): Borel carrier, countably (N−1)-rectifiable, θ_t ≥ 1 integer valued and locally integrable, ξ_t measurable and orienting the approximate tangent spaces a.e.
 (e) ⟨T, f, t⟩ := τ(M_t, θ_t, ξ_t) ∈ 𝒟_{N−1}(ℝ^P) is then an integer multiplicity current: im_calculus (b) with E = ℝ^P provides the current, the functional being sequentially continuous by local integrability.

4. (4.5(2): ⟨T, f, t⟩ = P_t for a.e. t.)
 (a) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{N−1}(ℝ^P), t ∈ ℝ and ε > 0. Let γ_ε : ℝ → [0, 1] equal 1 on (−∞, t − ε], 0 on [t, ∞), and be linear on [t − ε, t]. Then h := γ_ε ∘ f is Lipschitz, and its mollification h^{(σ)} := h ∗ φ_σ (Simon Ch. 2, §2) is smooth.
 (b) (∂T)(h^{(σ)}ω) = T(d(h^{(σ)}ω)) = T(dh^{(σ)} ∧ ω) + T(h^{(σ)} dω).
 (c) Since ξ(x) orients T_xM, ⟨ξ(x), dh^{(σ)}(x) ∧ ω(x)⟩ = ⟨ξ(x) ⌞ ∇^M h^{(σ)}(x), ω(x)⟩. As σ ↓ 0, ∇^M h^{(σ)} → ∇^M h weakly in L²(μ_T) on M. This is Simon's (1), checked on each C¹ piece N_j using the uniform convergence of h^{(σ)} to h. Hence lim_{σ↓0} T(dh^{(σ)} ∧ ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ξ ⌞ ∇^M h, ω⟩ dHᴺ.
 (d) By the chain rule (Simon's (4)), ∇^M h = γ_ε'(f)∇^M f Hᴺ-a.e. on M, since ∇^M f = 0 a.e. on level sets of f. Also h^{(σ)}ω → hω and h^{(σ)}dω → h dω uniformly, with supports in a fixed compact set. Using the representations of T and ∂T, (b) and (c) give
 ∫_{M'} θ' h⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{N−1} = −ε^{−1}∫_{M∩{t−ε<f<t}} θ⟨ξ ⌞ ∇^M f, ω⟩ dHᴺ + ∫_M θ h⟨dω, ξ⟩ dHᴺ.
 (e) Let ε ↓ 0. By dominated convergence (h → 1_{f<t}), the left side tends to B_t(ω) and the last term to A_t(dω). Apply Remark 4.2 (step 2) with g := θ⟨ξ ⌞ (∇^M f/|∇^M f|), ω⟩, split into positive and negative parts: the middle term tends to −∫_{M_t} θ⟨ξ_t, ω⟩ dH^{N−1} = −⟨T, f, t⟩(ω) for every t outside an L¹-null set F_ω. Hence ⟨T, f, t⟩(ω) = A_t(dω) − B_t(ω) = P_t(ω) for t ∉ F_ω.
 (f) Take a countable set Ω ⊆ 𝒟^{N−1}(ℝ^P) such that every ω is the limit of some ω_k ∈ Ω with supports in a fixed compact set and ω_k → ω, dω_k → dω uniformly (Simon: "by considering a countable dense set of ω"). Put F := ⋃_{ω ∈ Ω} F_ω, an L¹-null set. Both sides are continuous in ω for this convergence: |P_t(ω)| ≤ sup|dω| μ_T(K) + sup|ω| μ_{∂T}(K), and |⟨T, f, t⟩(ω)| ≤ sup|ω| ∫_{M_t∩K} θ dH^{N−1} < ∞ for a.e. t. So ⟨T, f, t⟩ = P_t for a.e. t.

5. (4.8: support.) For t as in steps 2–4, ⟨T, f, t⟩ = τ(M_t, θ_t, ξ_t) with M_t ⊆ f⁻¹(t). If tsupport ω ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ∅, then ω = 0 on M_t, so P_t(ω) = ⟨T, f, t⟩(ω) = 0. Together with step 3, P_t is integer multiplicity and vanishes on such ω for a.e. t; with the identity of step 1, which holds for every t, this proves (2).

6. (4.5(1) and measurability.) Let W be open.
 (a) For a.e. t, P_t = ⟨T, f, t⟩ is integer multiplicity with representation (M_t, θ_t, ξ_t). By the sibling mass_eq_measure (with U = ℝ^P), M_W(P_t) = ∫_{M_t∩W} θ dH^{N−1}.
 (b) By step 2(c) with g = θ1_W, the right side is an L¹-measurable function of t. So t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable.
 (c) Using |∇^M f| ≤ L Hᴺ-a.e. (f is L-Lipschitz) and mass_eq_measure for T: ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt = ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t∩W} θ dH^{N−1} dt = ∫_{M∩W} |∇^M f| θ dHᴺ ≤ L ∫_{M∩W} θ dHᴺ = L·μ_T(W) = L·M_W(T). This proves (1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Define P_t := ∂A_t − B_t for every t, with A_t, B_t the restrictions of T and ∂T to {f < t} (im_calculus (b)). This is the stated integral formula.
Coarea on M (Lemma 4.1): for a.e. t, M_t = M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t) is countably (m+1)-rectifiable with T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^M f, and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} g = ∫_M |∇^M f| g.
For a.e. t, ⟨T, f, t⟩ = τ(M_t, θ, ξ⌞∇^M f/|∇^M f|) is integer multiplicity (4.3–4.4).
Mollification and Remark 4.2 give ⟨T, f, t⟩ = P_t for a.e. t (4.5(2)); a countable dense family of forms makes the null set independent of ω.
P_t is carried by f⁻¹(t) (4.8). M_W(P_t) = ∫_{M_t∩W} θ is measurable in t, with integral ∫_{M∩W} |∇^M f| θ ≤ L·M_W(T) (4.5(1), mass_eq_measure).

subproblems.title: Push-forward of compactly supported integer multiplicity currents by a map that is C¹ near the support (Simon 6.2.23–2.29, 3.3–3.9)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there is a map push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following properties.
(A) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ O, and let (M, θ, ξ) be any integer multiplicity representation of Y. Then:
 (i) push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Here (ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x))(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ); in Lean, (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
 (ii) push Y is integer multiplicity.
 (iii) spt push Y ⊆ f(spt Y).
 (iv) For every real L with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for all y ∈ O, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y), as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n) * M(Y).
 (v) If ∂Y = 0, then ∂(push Y) = 0.
(B) push(Y₁ − Y₂) = push Y₁ − push Y₂ for all integer multiplicity Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact supports contained in O.
This is f_#Y of Simon 2.24(2) and 3.9.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, chapter-06.txt lines 404–530 and 770–860, with the area formula of Ch. 3, 2.4–2.6:
 • 2.23–2.24: push-forward and its boundary, and the explicit formula 2.24(2) for currents with locally finite mass and C¹ maps;
 • 2.27–2.29: homotopy estimate and mollified maps;
 • 3.3–3.9: push-forward of integer multiplicity currents by locally Lipschitz maps that are proper on the support; by 3.9, f_#T is integer multiplicity.
This is the result cited as (C3) in step 6 of the parent proof, with the properties listed there. The printed arguments are copied and specialised to a map f that is C¹ on an open set O containing the compact support. Two facts the source uses tacitly are proved in steps 2–3: additivity (B), and independence of the formula from the representation.

Notation. n = m + 1 and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. For an n-covector α and a linear map A, α ∘ ΛⁿA is the covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Av₁, …, Avₙ). For x ∈ O write Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. 𝒴 is the class of integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt Y compact and contained in O. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm.

1. (Preliminaries.)
 (a) Let v₁, …, vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and let V be the P×n matrix with columns vᵢ. By multilinearity and the alternating property, α(v₁, …, vₙ) = Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})·det(V_I), the sum over strictly increasing I : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, where V_I is the n×n submatrix of rows I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(v₁, …, vₙ)| ≤ |α|·(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(V_I)² = det(VᵀV), the Gram determinant, which is at most Π_i|vᵢ|² by Hadamard's inequality. Now let τ₁, …, τₙ be orthonormal, ζ = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ, and vᵢ := Aτᵢ. Then |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ζ⟩| = |α(Aτ₁, …, Aτₙ)| ≤ |α|·Π_i|Aτᵢ| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ. For n = 0 both sides equal |α|.
 (b) Let Y ∈ 𝒴, K := spt Y, and (M, θ, ξ) a representation of Y. Then Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. Indeed ℝ^P ∖ K is open and Y vanishes on forms supported there (vanish_off_support), so μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ K) = M_{ℝ^P∖K}(Y) = 0 (mass_eq_measure), and θ ≥ 1 on M.
 (c) Df is continuous on O ⊇ K, so Λ_K := sup_K ‖Df‖ < ∞. Also μ_Y(K) < ∞ by local finiteness of the weight.

2. (Definition and independence of the representation; Simon 2.24(2), 3.3.)
 (a) For Y ∈ 𝒴 with a representation (M, θ, ξ) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), let I(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
 (b) By 1(a)–(c) the integrand is bounded by θ·sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·1_K Hⁿ-a.e. on M. So the integral exists, is linear in ω, and |I(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K). Hence I is sequentially continuous on test forms (TestFormOnConverges gives uniform convergence) and defines a current.
 (c) I does not depend on the representation. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K, and put β(x) := χ(x)·(ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x)), a continuous compactly supported n-form. By 1(b), I(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. Mollifying β gives smooth β_k with supports in a fixed compact set and β_k → β uniformly. By dominated convergence ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k ∫_M θ⟨β_k, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k Y(β_k), which depends only on Y.
 (d) Define push Y := I for Y ∈ 𝒴, and push Y := 0 for Y ∉ 𝒴. Then (i) holds for every representation.

3. ((B) additivity.) Let Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒴 with supports K₁, K₂.
 (a) Y₁ − Y₂ is integer multiplicity (im_calculus (c)). It vanishes on every form whose support misses the compact set K₁ ∪ K₂ ⊆ O (vanish_off_support for Y₁ and Y₂). So spt(Y₁ − Y₂) is compact and contained in K₁ ∪ K₂ (support_of_vanishing), and Y₁ − Y₂ ∈ 𝒴.
 (b) Take χ = 1 near K₁ ∪ K₂ in step 2. Then push(Y₁ − Y₂)(ω) = lim_k (Y₁ − Y₂)(β_k) = lim_k Y₁(β_k) − lim_k Y₂(β_k) = push Y₁(ω) − push Y₂(ω).

4. ((iii) support; Simon 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴. f(K) is compact, since f is continuous on O ⊇ K. If tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅, then ω(f(x)) = 0 for x ∈ K, so by 1(b) the integrand in (i) vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. on M and push Y(ω) = 0. By support_of_vanishing (with U = ℝ^P and the compact set f(K)), spt push Y ⊆ f(K) = f(spt Y).

5. ((iv) mass; Simon 2.29.) Let L satisfy ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for y ∈ O. If O ≠ ∅ then L ≥ 0; if O = ∅ then K = ∅, μ_Y = 0 and push Y = 0. For every admissible ω (|ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y), by 1(a)(b): push Y(ω) ≤ ∫_M θ|ω(f(x))|·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_M θ dHⁿ = Lⁿ·μ_Y(ℝ^P) = Lⁿ·M(Y), by mass_eq_measure with W = ℝ^P. Taking the supremum, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).

6. ((ii) integer multiplicity; Simon 3.5–3.9.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with representation (M, θ, ξ). By 1(b) we may replace M by M ∩ K.
 (a) Choose an open V with K ⊆ V and closure(V) ⊆ O compact. Near each point of closure(V), f is C¹ and Lipschitz.
 (b) On M the tangential differential d^M f_x : T_xM → ℝ^P exists Hⁿ-a.e., and d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = Df(x)_#ξ(x), Df(x) restricted to T_xM (Simon Ch. 3, 2.2). So (i) reads push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)), d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ.
 (c) Let M₊ := {x ∈ M : J^M f(x) > 0}. Points with J^M f = 0 contribute nothing, since there d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = 0 (3.4). Since |d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| = J^M f(x), the area formula (Ch. 3, 2.5) gives (3.6):
 push Y(ω) = ∫_{f(M₊)} ⟨ω(y), Σ_{x ∈ f⁻¹(y)∩M₊} θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)|⟩ dHⁿ(y).
 (d) f(M₊) is countably n-rectifiable, as a union of Lipschitz images of the pieces of M on which f is Lipschitz. So for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ f(M₊) the approximate tangent space T_y f(M₊) exists. For Hⁿ-a.e. such y the set f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊ is finite (2.4), and each vector d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| with x in it equals ±η(y), for a unit simple n-vector η(y) orienting T_y f(M₊) (3.7).
 (e) Hence (3.8) Σ_x θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|…| = N(y)η(y) with N(y) ∈ ℤ. Replacing η by −η where N < 0, push Y = τ(f(M₊) ∩ {N ≠ 0}, |N|, η) (3.9).
 (f) The multiplicity is locally integrable: ∫_{f(M₊)} |N| dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{f(M₊)} Σ_x θ(x) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_M θ J^M f dHⁿ ≤ Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K) < ∞ (area formula 2.5).
 (g) Choosing Borel versions of the carrier, N and η, this is an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P representing push Y. So push Y is integer multiplicity.

7. ((v) boundary; Simon 2.24(1), 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with ∂Y = 0, and V as in step 6.
 (a) Let χ₁ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ₁ = 1 on a neighbourhood of closure(V), and f_σ := (χ₁f) ∗ φ_σ for σ > 0 (mollification). Then f_σ is smooth on ℝ^P, and f_σ → f, Df_σ → Df uniformly on closure(V) as σ ↓ 0, because f is C¹ near closure(V).
 (b) For the smooth map g := f_σ, Simon 2.23 defines g_#Y(ω) := Y(ζ g^#ω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P), ζ = 1 near K; the value does not depend on ζ.
 (c) By 2.24(1), ∂g_#Y = g_#∂Y = 0. Indeed ∂g_#Y(ω) = Y(ζ g^#dω) = Y(ζ d(g^#ω)) = Y(d(ζ g^#ω)) − Y(dζ ∧ g^#ω) = (∂Y)(ζ g^#ω) − 0 = 0, because dζ ∧ g^#ω vanishes near K = spt Y.
 (d) By 2.24(2), g_#Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f_σ(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf_σ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ. As σ ↓ 0 this tends to push Y(ω), by dominated convergence (uniform convergence on K and the bound of step 2).
 (e) Hence ∂(push Y)(ω) = push Y(dω) = lim_σ f_{σ#}Y(dω) = lim_σ ∂(f_{σ#}Y)(ω) = 0 for every ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: For Y with compact support K ⊆ O, push Y(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ (2.24(2)) is a current. It does not depend on the representation (approximate the continuous form χ·f^#ω by smooth forms), and push Y := 0 otherwise.
Additivity follows from independence of the representation. The support lies in f(K), since the integrand vanishes off f⁻¹(spt ω).
Mass: |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ (Cauchy–Binet, Hadamard) gives M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).
Integer multiplicity by the area formula: push Y = τ(f(M₊), |N|, ±η) with N integer valued (3.6–3.9).
If ∂Y = 0 then ∂(push Y) = 0: push Y is the weak limit of push-forwards by smooth mollified maps, which commute with ∂ (2.24(1), 2.29).

subproblems.title: A map fixing the support of an integer multiplicity current fixes its approximate tangent planes and orientation almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be differentiable at every point of O (DifferentiableOn ℝ f O) with f(y) = y for every y ∈ spt T ∩ O. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ O (Hⁿ = μHE[n]): f(x) = x, and ⟨α ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ = ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ for every n-covector α. In Lean the last identity reads R.orient x (α.compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) = R.orient x α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U O : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsOpen O → R.Represents T → DifferentiableOn ℝ f O → (∀ y ∈ T.support ∩ O, f y = y) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ O)), f x = x ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, R.orient x (α.compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) = R.orient x α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7(a)–(c) of the parent proof ("π fixes S_i near B_G"). It is stated here for a general integer multiplicity current T, open set O and map f in place of S_i⌞B_G, B_{2G} and π_i. The good set M' := M ∩ O ∩ spt T replaces M_i ∩ B_G ∩ A_i; the parent applies the result with spt S_i ⊆ A_i.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n E x Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_Q φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0, for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4).

1. (Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0.) spt T = U ∖ Z_T with Z_T open (SimonGMT isOpen_zeroRegion), so V := U ∖ spt T = U ∩ Z_T is open and V ⊆ U.
 (a) Every form ω admissible for M_V(T) has tsupport ω ⊆ V, which is disjoint from spt T, so T(ω) = 0 by the sibling vanish_off_support. Hence M_V(T) = 0.
 (b) By the sibling mass_eq_measure, μ_R(V) = M_V(T) = 0, where μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M.
 (c) Since θ ≥ 1 on M (field mult_pos), Hⁿ(M ∩ V) ≤ μ_R(V) = 0. As M ⊆ U, M ∖ spt T = M ∩ V.

2. (The good set.) Put M' := M ∩ O ∩ spt T. It is Borel, since spt T = U ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ Z_T). Moreover M' ⊆ M ∩ O and Hⁿ((M ∩ O) ∖ M') ≤ Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0 by step 1.

3. (Locality of approximate tangent spaces; parent 7(a).) Let x ∈ O and Q be a subspace with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q.
 (a) Let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt φ ⊆ B_ρ(0), and d := dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 0 (d := ∞ if O = ℝ^P). For 0 < r < d/ρ, η_{x,r}(y) ∈ B_ρ(0) implies |y − x| < rρ < d, i.e. y ∈ O. So φ = 0 on η_{x,r}(M ∖ O), and since η_{x,r} is injective, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M∩O)} φ dHⁿ.
 (b) η_{x,r}(M ∩ O) is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M') and η_{x,r}((M ∩ O) ∖ M'). Since η_{x,r} is a similarity with ratio r⁻¹, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(E)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for every E, so the second set is Hⁿ-null by step 2.
 (c) Therefore ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} φ dHⁿ for all r ∈ (0, d/ρ), and both families have the same limit ∫_Q φ dHⁿ.

4. (Good points.)
 (a) By the field orients of R, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is a subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q_x. That is, there are an orthonormal basis τ₁, …, τₙ of Q_x and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for all α.
 (b) By step 2, Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ O also lies in M'. Fix x ∈ M ∩ O with both properties.
 (c) Then x ∈ spt T ∩ O, so f(x) = x; and by step 3, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q_x.
 (d) If n = 0, then α ∘ Λ⁰Df(x) = α for every 0-covector and there is nothing more to prove. Assume n ≥ 1.

5. (Secant directions; parent 7(b).) Every unit vector v ∈ Q_x is the limit of (z_k − x)/|z_k − x| for some z_k ∈ M' ∖ {x} with z_k → x.
 (a) Suppose not. Then there are ε', r' > 0 such that |(z − x)/|z − x| − v| ≥ ε' for all z ∈ M' with 0 < |z − x| < r'.
 (b) Let Ω := {w : 1/2 < |w| < 1, |w/|w| − v| < ε'}, an open set containing w₀ := (3/4)v. For 0 < r < r', η_{x,r}(M') ∩ Ω = ∅: if w = (z − x)/r ∈ Ω with z ∈ M', then 0 < |z − x| = r|w| < r' and (z − x)/|z − x| = w/|w|, contradicting (a).
 (c) Choose φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, spt φ ⊆ Ω and φ(w₀) = 1. Then ∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} φ dHⁿ = 0 for 0 < r < r', so by step 4(c) ∫_{Q_x} φ dHⁿ = 0.
 (d) But w₀ ∈ Q_x, φ > 1/2 on a neighbourhood N of w₀, and Hⁿ(N ∩ Q_x) > 0, because the support of Hⁿ⌞Q_x is Q_x (SimonGMT support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule; Hⁿ⌞Q_x is Lebesgue measure on the n-plane Q_x). Hence ∫_{Q_x} φ dHⁿ > 0, a contradiction.

6. (Df(x) = id on Q_x; parent 7(c).) Since x ∈ O and O is open, f is differentiable at x: f(z) − f(x) − Df(x)(z − x) = o(|z − x|) as z → x.
 (a) For z_k as in step 5, z_k ∈ M' ⊆ spt T ∩ O, so f(z_k) = z_k; and f(x) = x.
 (b) Hence (I − Df(x))(z_k − x) = o(|z_k − x|), i.e. (I − Df(x))u_k → 0 for u_k := (z_k − x)/|z_k − x| → v.
 (c) By continuity of the linear map I − Df(x), (I − Df(x))v = 0. By linearity, Df(x)w = w for every w ∈ Q_x.

7. (Conclusion.) For every n-covector α, ⟨α ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ = s·(α ∘ ΛⁿDf(x))(τ₁, …, τₙ) = s·α(Df(x)τ₁, …, Df(x)τₙ) = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩, and f(x) = x. The points x of step 4 form a set of full Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ O)-measure, so the conclusion holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ O. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0 (vanish_off_support and mass_eq_measure), so the good set M' = M ∩ O ∩ spt T has full measure in M ∩ O.
At points of O the approximate tangent space of M' equals that of M, because the blow-ups differ by null sets.
Every unit v in T_xM is a limit of secant directions from M'; otherwise a test function supported in a cone contradicts ∫_{T_xM} φ > 0.
f fixes M' and is differentiable at x, so Df(x)v = v on T_xM. Hence ΛⁿDf(x) fixes the orientation ξ(x) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ, and f(x) = x.

subproblems.title: Subadditivity of the weights of integer multiplicity currents: μ_{X + cY} ≤ μ_X + μ_Y for |c| ≤ 1
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and X, Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with integer multiplicity representations R_X, R_Y, R_Z in U (IMRep U n). Let c ∈ ℝ with |c| ≤ 1, and suppose Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then the weights satisfy μ_Z ≤ μ_X + μ_Y as measures on ℝ^P, where μ_• := R_•.measure = θ_•Hⁿ⌞M_•. That is, μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X Y Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (RX RY RZ : IMRep U n) (c : ℝ), IsOpen U → |c| ≤ 1 → RX.Represents X → RY.Represents Y → RZ.Represents Z → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = X ω + c * Y ω) → RZ.measure ≤ RX.measure + RY.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0, fact (F4) of the parent proof: "μ_{A±B}(E) ≤ μ_A(E) + μ_B(E) for every Borel E: for open E because M_E(A ± B) ≤ M_E(A) + M_E(B) (each admissible ω gives (A ± B)(ω) ≤ M_E(A) + M_E(B), as ±ω is admissible), and for Borel E by outer regularity of these locally finite Borel measures". Here it is stated for Z = X + cY with |c| ≤ 1; c = ±1 gives A ± B.

Notation. μ_X := R_X.measure = θ_XHⁿ⌞M_X, and similarly for Y and Z. M_V = massOn V is the supremum of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y (Euclidean coefficient norm).

1. (Mass triangle on open sets.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open and ω admissible for M_V. Then −ω is admissible too, since tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω and |−α| = |α|. So X(ω) ≤ M_V(X) and |Y(ω)| = max(Y(ω), Y(−ω)) ≤ M_V(Y), in [0, ∞] (SimonGMT le_massOn). Hence Z(ω) = X(ω) + cY(ω) ≤ M_V(X) + |c||Y(ω)| ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y), so ofReal Z(ω) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y). Taking the supremum, M_V(Z) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y). (This step is the comparator-accepted declaration lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq with G := V.)

2. (Open subsets of U.) For open V ⊆ U the sibling mass_eq_measure gives M_V(•) = μ_•(V) for • ∈ {X, Y, Z}. With step 1, μ_Z(V) ≤ μ_X(V) + μ_Y(V).

3. (Concentration on U.) The carriers lie in U, so μ_•(E) = μ_•(E ∩ U) for every Borel E.

4. (Exhaustion and local finiteness.) For k ≥ 1 let
 K_k := {x ∈ U : |x| ≤ k, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/k} (K_k := closedBall(0, k) if U = ℝ^P),
 V_k := {x : |x| < k + 1, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/(k + 1)} (V_k := B_{k+1}(0) if U = ℝ^P).
 Then K_k is compact, K_k ⊆ V_k ⊆ K_{k+1} ⊆ U, V_k is open and ⋃_k K_k = U. Since closure(V_k) ⊆ K_{k+1} is a compact subset of U, μ_•(V_k) ≤ μ_•(K_{k+1}) < ∞ (IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult).

5. (Borel subsets of K_k.) Let E ⊆ K_k be Borel and δ > 0.
 (a) λ := (μ_X + μ_Y + μ_Z)⌞V_k is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P, hence outer regular. So there is an open O ⊇ E with λ(O) ≤ λ(E) + δ.
 (b) Put O' := O ∩ V_k, an open set with E ⊆ O' ⊆ U. Then μ_•(O' ∖ E) ≤ λ(O ∖ E) = λ(O) − λ(E) ≤ δ for each •.
 (c) By step 2, μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_Z(O') ≤ μ_X(O') + μ_Y(O') ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E) + 2δ. Letting δ ↓ 0, μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E).

6. (All Borel sets.) For Borel E, the sets E ∩ K_k increase to E ∩ U. By step 5 and continuity from below, μ_Z(E ∩ U) ≤ μ_X(E ∩ U) + μ_Y(E ∩ U), i.e. μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E) by step 3. An inequality between measures may be checked on measurable sets (Measure.le_iff), so μ_Z ≤ μ_X + μ_Y. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_V(X + cY) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y) for open V, since ±ω are both admissible and |c| ≤ 1. With mass_eq_measure this is μ_Z(V) ≤ μ_X(V) + μ_Y(V) for open V ⊆ U.
All three weights live on U and are finite on compact subsets of U.
Outer regularity of the finite measure (μ_X + μ_Y + μ_Z)⌞V_k extends the inequality to Borel subsets of K_k.
Exhaust U by compact sets and use continuity from below.

subproblems.title: Comparison of a minimizer in A with a cycle pushed into A by a near-isometric C¹ retraction (Simon 7.2.4 (9) with Remark 7.2.5(2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, A ⊆ ℝ^P, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in A (IsMinimizingIn S A) with spt S ⊆ A. Let G > 0 with closedBall(0, G) ⊆ U, and L ≥ 0. Let π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be C¹ on B_{2G}(0), with π(B_{2G}(0)) ⊆ A, π(y) = y for y ∈ A ∩ B_{2G}(0), and |π(y)| ≤ 2|y| and |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ L|y − z| for y, z ∈ B_{2G}(0). Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with ∂Y = 0, spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ B_{G/2}(0). Then M_{B_G(0)}(S) ≤ Lⁿ·M_{B_G(0)}(S + Y). Here S + Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means S − (0 − Y|_U), with Y|_U := Y.restrictDomain (U ⊆ ℝ^P), and Lⁿ is read as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (π : Euclid P → Euclid P) (G L : ℝ), IsOpen U → IsMinimizingIn S A → S.support ⊆ A → 0 < G → closedBall (0 : Euclid P) G ⊆ U → 0 ≤ L → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 π (ball 0 (2 * G)) → MapsTo π (ball 0 (2 * G)) A → (∀ y ∈ A ∩ ball 0 (2 * G), π y = y) → (∀ y ∈ ball 0 (2 * G), ‖π y‖ ≤ 2 * ‖y‖) → (∀ y ∈ ball 0 (2 * G), ∀ z ∈ ball 0 (2 * G), ‖π y - π z‖ ≤ L * ‖y - z‖) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y → Y.boundary = 0 → IsCompact Y.support → Y.support ⊆ ball 0 (G / 2) → S.massOn (ball 0 G) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ (m + 1)) * (S - (0 - Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U))).massOn (ball 0 G)

Source: steps 6 and 7 of the parent proof, stated for one index: the competitor Z_i = S_i + π_{i#}Y_i, minimality of S_i in A_i, π_{i#}Q_i = Q_i and the estimate (I). The parent applies it with S = S_i, A = A_i, U = U_i, π = π_i, L = 1 + η and Y = Y_i, where spt Y_i ⊆ B_{G/3}(0).

Siblings used: pushforward (PF), orientation_fixed (OF), measure_subadditive (F4), mass_eq_measure (M), vanish_off_support (V), im_calculus (b) restriction and (c) differences, restrict_domain_im (RD), support_of_vanishing (SV).

Notation. n := m + 1 and B_r := ball(0, r). ι is the inclusion of 𝒟ⁿ(U) into 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (same form). For currents A, B in one domain, A + B := A − (0 − B), so (A + B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(ω). The zero current is integer multiplicity, since it equals A − A for any integer multiplicity A (im_calculus (c)).

1. (Derivative bound.) π is C¹ and L-Lipschitz on the open ball B_{2G}, with L ≥ 0. So ‖Dπ(y)‖ ≤ L for y ∈ B_{2G} (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn).

2. (Q := S⌞B_G as a current in ℝ^P.) Let (M, θ, ξ) represent S; S is integer multiplicity by the first part of IsMinimizingIn.
 (a) By im_calculus (b) (with U and E = B_G), (M ∩ B_G, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity triple in U. Since M ∩ B_G ⊆ closedBall(0, G), a compact subset of U, its multiplicity is integrable over every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P: ∫_{M∩B_G∩K} θ ≤ ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,G)} θ < ∞.
 (b) So the same data form an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P. By im_calculus (b) (with ℝ^P and E = ℝ^P) it represents a current Q ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), with carrier M ∩ B_G and weight μ_Q = μ_S⌞B_G.
 (Q1) If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ B_G, then S(ω) = Q(ιω). Both are ∫θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ, over M and over M ∩ B_G respectively, and ω = 0 on M ∖ B_G.
 (Q2) spt Q ⊆ K_Q := closedBall(0, G) ∩ spt S. This set is compact (it equals closedBall(0, G) ∖ Z_S, as closedBall(0, G) ⊆ U) and contained in A ∩ B_{2G} (as spt S ⊆ A). Indeed Hⁿ(M ∖ spt S) = 0, because μ_S(U ∖ spt S) = 0 by V and M and θ ≥ 1. If tsupport ω ∩ K_Q = ∅, then ω(x) = 0 for every x ∈ (M ∩ B_G) ∩ spt S. So the integrand of Q(ω) vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ B_G, and Q(ω) = 0. SV gives spt Q ⊆ K_Q, and spt Q is compact.

3. (Push-forward.) Apply PF with O := B_{2G} and f := π, which is C¹ on O. This gives push with properties (i)–(v) and (B). Q and Y are in its domain: both are integer multiplicity with compact supports contained in B_{2G}, since spt Q ⊆ closedBall(0, G) and spt Y ⊆ B_{G/2}.
 (Q3) push Q = Q.
 (a) Apply OF to Q with its representation (M ∩ B_G, θ, ξ), U := ℝ^P, O := B_{2G} and f := π, which is differentiable on O. Its hypothesis holds: for y ∈ spt Q ∩ B_{2G} we have y ∈ spt S ⊆ A, so π(y) = y.
 (b) Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ B_G (⊆ B_{2G}): π(x) = x and ⟨α ∘ ΛⁿDπ(x), ξ(x)⟩ = ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ for all α.
 (c) By PF (i), push Q(ω) = ∫_{M∩B_G} θ⟨ω(π(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDπ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩B_G} θ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ = Q(ω).

4. (Additivity.) 0 − Y is integer multiplicity with spt(0 − Y) = spt Y, since (0 − Y)(ω) = −Y(ω) and so the zero regions coincide; and spt 0 = ∅.
 (a) PF (B) with (0, 0) gives push 0 = push 0 − push 0, hence push 0 = 0.
 (b) PF (B) with (0, Y) gives push(0 − Y) = 0 − push Y.
 (c) PF (B) with (Q, 0 − Y) gives push(Q + Y) = push Q − push(0 − Y).
 (d) Using (Q3), push(Q + Y)(ω) = Q(ω) + push Y(ω) for every ω.

5. (The competitor; parent step 6.) Let Z := S + (push Y)|_U ∈ 𝒟_n(U), where (push Y)|_U is the restriction to the domain U (restrictDomain).
 (a) (push Y)|_U is integer multiplicity by RD and PF (ii), so Z is integer multiplicity by im_calculus (c).
 (b) ∂Z = ∂S, because ∂((push Y)|_U)(ω) = push Y(ι dω) = ∂(push Y)(ιω) = 0, by PF (v) and ∂Y = 0.
 (c) Let K_π := π(spt Y). It is compact, since π is continuous on B_{2G} ⊇ spt Y. It is contained in A ∩ B_G, since π maps B_{2G} into A and |π(y)| ≤ 2|y| < G for y ∈ spt Y ⊆ B_{G/2}. In particular K_π ⊆ U.
 (d) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ∩ K_π = ∅: (Z − S)(ω) = push Y(ιω) = 0, by V and spt push Y ⊆ K_π (PF (iii)). By SV, spt(Z − S) ⊆ K_π and spt(Z − S) is compact. So spt(Z − S) is a compact subset of A ∩ B_G.
 (e) B_G is open with closure closedBall(0, G) compact and contained in U. Minimality of S in A (IsMinimizingIn, with W := B_G and the competitor Z) gives M_{B_G}(S) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z).

6. (Estimate of M_{B_G}(Z); parent (I).)
 (a) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_G: Z(ω) = S(ω) + push Y(ιω) = Q(ιω) + push Y(ιω) = push(Q + Y)(ιω), by (Q1) and step 4. Since ιω is admissible for M_{B_G} in ℝ^P whenever ω is, M_{B_G}(Z) ≤ M_{B_G}(push(Q + Y)) ≤ M(push(Q + Y)).
 (b) Q + Y is integer multiplicity, with compact support in K_Q ∪ spt Y ⊆ B_{2G}: it vanishes on forms supported off this compact set, and SV applies. By PF (iv) and step 1, M(push(Q + Y)) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Q + Y).
 (c) M(Q + Y) = M_{B_G}(Q + Y). By F4 (with c = 1), μ_{Q+Y} ≤ μ_Q + μ_Y. Also μ_Q(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) = 0, since its carrier M ∩ B_G lies in B_G, and μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) ≤ μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ spt Y) = 0 by V and M. So μ_{Q+Y}(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) = 0, and by M, M(Q + Y) = μ_{Q+Y}(ℝ^P) = μ_{Q+Y}(B_G) = M_{B_G}(Q + Y).
 (d) M_{B_G}(Q + Y) ≤ M_{B_G}(S + Y|_U). Every ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) admissible for M_{B_G} lies in 𝒟ⁿ(U), as tsupport ω' ⊆ B_G ⊆ U, and (Q + Y)(ω') = S(ω') + Y(ω') = (S + Y|_U)(ω') by (Q1).

7. (Conclusion.) M_{B_G}(S) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z) ≤ M(push(Q + Y)) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Q + Y) = Lⁿ·M_{B_G}(Q + Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M_{B_G}(S + Y|_U), with Lⁿ read as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n). ∎
proof_key_steps: ‖Dπ‖ ≤ L on B_{2G}. Q := S⌞B_G is an integer multiplicity current in ℝ^P that agrees with S on forms supported in B_G, with compact support in B̄_G ∩ spt S ⊆ A.
By orientation_fixed and the push-forward formula, π_#Q = Q; by additivity, π_#(Q + Y) = Q + π_#Y.
Z := S + π_#Y is an integer multiplicity competitor with ∂Z = ∂S and spt(Z − S) ⊆ π(spt Y), a compact subset of A ∩ B_G. Minimality gives M_{B_G}(S) ≤ M_{B_G}(Z).
M_{B_G}(Z) ≤ M(π_#(Q + Y)) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Q + Y), and M(Q + Y) = M_{B_G}(Q + Y) = M_{B_G}(S + Y) by measure subadditivity off B_G.

subproblems.title: Choice of a common good level for countably many a.e. properties, a summable family of slice masses and countably many measures
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and a < b real numbers. Let g_i : ℝ → [0, ∞] (i ∈ ℕ) be a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to (a, b), with Σ_i ∫_{(a,b)} g_i dt < ∞. Let μ_i (i ∈ ℕ) be measures on ℝ^P and h : ℝ^P → ℝ a measurable function with μ_i({a < h < b}) < ∞ for every i. Let good_i (i ∈ ℕ) be predicates on ℝ, each holding for L¹-a.e. t. Then there is t ∈ (a, b) such that good_i(t) holds for every i, Σ_i g_i(t) < ∞, and μ_i({h = t}) = 0 for every i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (μ : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ) (good : ℕ → ℝ → Prop) (a b : ℝ), a < b → Measurable h → (∀ i, AEMeasurable (g i) (volume.restrict (Ioo a b))) → (∑' i, ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g i t) ≠ ∞ → (∀ i, μ i {x | a < h x ∧ h x < b} ≠ ∞) → (∀ i, ∀ᵐ t, good i t) → ∃ t ∈ Ioo a b, (∀ i, good i t) ∧ (∑' i, g i t) ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ i, μ i {x | h x = t} = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof: "Choose α ∈ (0, 1) outside the union of the following null sets: the levels where for some i the slice is not IM or the slice identity fails (countably many null sets); the levels with Σ_i M(P_i(α)) = ∞; and the levels with μ_{S_{φ₁(i)}}(Σ_α) > 0 for some i (for each i these are countably many, because the Σ_α are pairwise disjoint subsets of … finite μ-measure)". Here the levels are t ∈ (a, b), the level sets are {h = t}, and the predicates good_i are abstract. λ denotes Lebesgue measure on ℝ.

1. (Failures of the predicates.) For each i, N_i := {t : ¬good_i(t)} is λ-null by hypothesis. So N := ⋃_i N_i is λ-null, as a countable union (Mathlib ae_all_iff).

2. (Summability.) Let λ_ab := λ⌞(a, b). Each g_i is λ_ab-a.e. measurable, so ∫_{(a,b)} Σ_i g_i dλ = Σ_i ∫_{(a,b)} g_i dλ < ∞ (lintegral_tsum), and Σ_i g_i is λ_ab-a.e. measurable. A non-negative a.e.-measurable function with finite integral is finite a.e. (ae_lt_top'). So N' := {t ∈ (a, b) : Σ_i g_i(t) = ∞} is λ-null.

3. (Atoms of the level sets.) Fix i and put ν_i := μ_i⌞{a < h < b}, a finite measure by hypothesis and hence s-finite.
 (a) Since h is measurable, the sets {h = t} are disjoint and measurable, and at most countably many of them have positive ν_i-measure. So C_i := {t : ν_i({h = t}) > 0} is countable (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos).
 (b) For t ∈ (a, b), {h = t} ⊆ {a < h < b}, so μ_i({h = t}) = ν_i({h = t}). Hence μ_i({h = t}) = 0 for t ∈ (a, b) ∖ C_i.
 (c) C := ⋃_i C_i is countable, hence λ-null.

4. (Choice.) λ((a, b)) = b − a > 0, while N ∪ N' ∪ C is λ-null. So there is t ∈ (a, b) ∖ (N ∪ N' ∪ C). For this t: good_i(t) for all i (t ∉ N), Σ_i g_i(t) < ∞ (t ∉ N'), and μ_i({h = t}) = 0 for all i (t ∉ C). ∎
proof_key_steps: The failures of the predicates form a countable union of null sets.
Σ_i g_i has finite integral over (a, b), hence is finite a.e.
For each i, at most countably many level sets {h = t} carry μ_i-mass, because μ_i⌞{a < h < b} is finite.
(a, b) has positive measure, so some t avoids all exceptional sets.

subproblems.title: Mass equals weight for integer multiplicity currents (reused accepted dtc_mass_eq_measure)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm (the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) and μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure; both sides are taken in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → R.Represents T → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dtc_mass_eq_measure (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.mass_eq_measure-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit bff81d31ecb43002d1bfc77f510d3463c6be155f). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. Role in the parent proof: It is fact (F1) of the parent proof, M_O(Y) = μ_Y(O) for open O ⊆ V, and one of the parent node's inherited dependencies (M). It is listed here as a child so that it is a declared prerequisite of this node and of its children. The parent uses it in steps 5, 7 and 8 to turn masses on B_G, W, W₀, ℝ^P into weights. The siblings flat_decomposition, slicing, pushforward, orientation_fixed, measure_subadditive and retraction_comparison use it too. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof) together with 2.4–2.8 (lines 222–283); this is the identity "M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W" quoted at the start of the parent proof. Notation: for α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P}; e^I ∈ Λⁿ is the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; μ := μ_R, so μ(B) = ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. By definition M_W(T) = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 ∀y} ("admissible" forms).
1. Algebraic lemma. Let τ₁,…,τₙ ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, σ ∈ {1, −1}, and let ζ ∈ Λₙ (MultiVector) satisfy ζ(α) = σ·α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all α. For increasing I put d_I := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b} = e^I(τ₁,…,τₙ). (a) Expanding each τ_b in the standard basis and using multilinearity and the alternating property (terms with a repeated basis vector vanish, the others are grouped by their increasing rearrangement with the sign of the sorting permutation) gives α(τ₁,…,τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·d_I for every α. (b) By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I d_I² = det(AᵀA), A the P×n matrix with columns τ_b; AᵀA = I_n by orthonormality, so Σ_I d_I² = 1. (c) Hence, by Cauchy–Schwarz, |ζ(α)| = |Σ_I α(e_I)d_I| ≤ |α| for every α. (d) Put α_ζ := Σ_I ζ(e^I)·e^I (a linear function of ζ). Since e^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing I, J, α_ζ(e_J) = ζ(e^J) = σd_J, hence |α_ζ| = (Σ_J d_J²)^{1/2} = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = Σ_I ζ(e^I)² = Σ_I d_I² = 1.
2. By the field `orients` of R there is an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M such that for every x ∈ M ∖ Z, ξ(x) satisfies the hypothesis of step 1 (τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on M (ξ is, ω is continuous, evaluation is continuous bilinear) and bounded by θ(x)·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}(x) off Z; since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, ∫_{M∩tsupport ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (field `locallyIntegrable_mult`). So T(ω) is the integral of an integrable function.
3. Upper bound. Let ω be admissible. For x ∈ M ∖ Z, step 1(c) and tsupport ω ⊆ W give θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) ≤ θ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_W(x). Integrating, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ(W), so ofReal T(ω) ≤ μ(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. Lower bound on a compact set. Let K ⊆ W be compact and 0 < ε < 1. Fix s > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ s} ⊆ W; K₁ is compact, K₁ ⊆ U, so μ(K₁) < ∞.
 (a) The open sets V_m := {dist(·, K) < 1/m} decrease to K and μ(K₁) < ∞, so for some m with 1/m < s the open set V := V_m satisfies K ⊆ V ⊆ K₁ and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.
 (b) Let α(y) := α_{ξ(y)} (step 1(d)); α is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so there is a Borel map α̃ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ with α̃ = α μ-a.e. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, μ-null subsets of M are Hⁿ-null; let Z' be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing Z ∪ ({α̃ ≠ α} ∩ M). For y ∈ M ∖ Z' we have |α̃(y)| = 1 and ξ(y)(α̃(y)) = 1. By Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure μ⌞K₁ on ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; Λⁿ is identified with ℝ^{C(P,n)} through the coefficients α(e_I)) there is a compact F₀ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ F₀) < ε/2 and α̃|_{F₀} continuous; by inner regularity there is a compact F ⊆ (F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z' (a Borel set, M being Borel) with μ(((F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z') ∖ F) < ε/2. As μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and μ(Z') = 0, μ(K ∖ F) < ε; moreover F ⊆ M ∖ Z', α̃|_F is continuous, and |α̃| = 1, ξ(·)(α̃(·)) = 1 on F.
 (c) By the Tietze extension theorem (coefficientwise) α̃|_F extends to a continuous β₀ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ. Let r(v) := v / max(1, |v|), the continuous radial retraction of (Λⁿ, |·|) onto its closed unit ball, and β := r ∘ β₀. Then β is continuous, |β| ≤ 1, and β = α̃ on F (because |α̃| = 1 there).
 (d) Let φ_δ be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, support in B_δ(0)) and β_δ := β * φ_δ (coefficientwise convolution). Then β_δ is smooth, |β_δ(y)| ≤ ∫|β(y − z)|φ_δ(z) dz ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm, Minkowski's integral inequality), and β_δ → β uniformly on compact sets as δ ↓ 0 (β is uniformly continuous on compact sets). Fix δ with |β_δ − β| ≤ ε on F.
 (e) Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χβ_δ. Then ω is smooth with compact tsupport ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and |ω| ≤ 1: ω is admissible.
 (f) Since χ = 1 on F ⊆ K and ω = 0 off V, T(ω) = ∫_{F} θ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ + ∫_{M∩(V∖F)} θ χ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ. For y ∈ F (so y ∈ M ∖ Z'): ξ(y)(β_δ(y)) = ξ(y)(α̃(y)) + ξ(y)(β_δ(y) − β(y)) ≥ 1 − |β_δ(y) − β(y)| ≥ 1 − ε by step 1(c) and (b). For y ∈ (M ∩ (V ∖ F)) ∖ Z, |χ(y)ξ(y)(β_δ(y))| ≤ 1. Since μ(V ∖ F) ≤ μ(V ∖ K) + μ(K ∖ F) < 2ε, we get T(ω) ≥ (1 − ε)μ(F) − 2ε ≥ (1 − ε)(μ(K) − ε) − 2ε ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3).
 (g) Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(ω) ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3); letting ε ↓ 0 gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(K).
5. Exhaustion. W is open, so W = ⋃_m K_m with the increasing compact sets K_m := {y ∈ W : |y| ≤ m, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/m} (K_m := {|y| ≤ m} if W = ℝ^P). By continuity of μ from below and step 4, μ(W) = sup_m μ(K_m) ≤ M_W(T). Together with step 3, M_W(T) = μ(W) in [0, ∞].
proof_key_steps: A unit simple n-vector ζ satisfies |ζ(α)| ≤ |α|_Euclid (Cauchy–Binet) and has a dual covector α_ζ, linear in ζ, with |α_ζ| = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = 1.
Upper bound: for every admissible ω, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W).
Lower bound on compact K ⊆ W: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, mollification and a cutoff give an admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ μ_R(K) − ε(μ_R(K) + 3).
Exhaust the open set W by compact sets to conclude M_W(T) = μ_R(W).

subproblems.title: A current vanishes on forms supported off its support (reused accepted dtc_vanish_off_support)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, where spt S = U ∖ Z_S and Z_S is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Then S(ω) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0

This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 44ef61f79e2168134f8a5a6d6520baba56052d67). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. Role in the parent proof: It is the parent node's inherited dependency (V), behind fact (F3): a current vanishes on test forms supported off its support. It is listed here as a child so that it is a declared prerequisite of this node and of its children. The parent uses it for X = S − C (spt X ⊆ K, step 6), for Y_i on the open set O' (step 8(b)) and for μ_X(Σ) = 0 (step 8(c)). The siblings pushforward, orientation_fixed and retraction_comparison use it too. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of the zero region of S, hence covered by finitely many open sets on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction of representations, differences of integer multiplicity currents (reused accepted cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub)
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)

It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. Role in the parent proof: Part (b) is fact (F5) of the parent proof: restricting a representation to the open set W = W_α (or B_G) gives integer multiplicity currents R̃_i = R_i⌞W and (∂R_i)⌞W (step 5), and S⌞B_G in the sibling retraction_comparison. Part (c) is fact (G): differences of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity, hence so are sums A − (0 − B) and the zero current A − A. Part (c) subsumes the parent's inherited dependency dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub, without its hypothesis n > 0. Parts (a) and (d) are used inside the siblings. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃_B(x) = ξ̃_A(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function).
3. (Data.) Put O := (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀, k := θ_A − εθ_B ∈ ℤ on O, and
 M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀,
 θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued),
 ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel).
For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x) (on O with k = 0 both sides vanish; on O with k ≠ 0, θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A = kξ̃_A = |k| sign(k)ξ̃_A; the other cases are immediate).
4. (Representation.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ against both sides of step 3 (N₀ is null; all integrands are integrable by (d), since θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}):
 ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A} θ_A⟨ω, ξ_A⟩ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
5. (Structure fields.) M is Borel, M ⊆ M_A ∪ M_B ⊆ U, and M is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ is Borel and ℕ-valued with θ ≥ 1 on M (|k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0), and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K} θ_A dHⁿ + ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. Let x be such a point, x ∉ N₀. If x ∈ M_A, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_A(x) and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A ∖ M_B and O, using ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x)), a unit orientation of Q_A(x) by (P5). If x ∈ M_B ∖ M_A, ζ(x) = −ξ_B(x) is a unit orientation of Q_B(x), the approximate tangent space of M at x. Hence the orientation field holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B, and A − B is integer multiplicity. ∎

Consequences used by siblings. (i) By (c), 0 = B − B, −B = 0 − B and A + B := A − (0 − B) are integer multiplicity whenever A, B are, hence so is every finite integer combination of integer multiplicity currents in an open set. (ii) The zero current is integer multiplicity even when no integer multiplicity current is given: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; the positivity, integrability, measurability and orientation fields hold vacuously because μHE restricted to ∅ is the zero measure; the representing integral over ∅ is 0). This is a direct check, not part of the Lean statement; siblings repeat it where needed. (iii) By (d), for an IMRep R, (R.measure, R.orient) satisfies the a.e. bound |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| required by the sibling slicing.
Remark (reuse; not a proof step). Comparator-accepted DAG declarations cover parts of this proof: regcomp_approx_tangent_locality (and rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset, same type) is part (a) with A := M, B := M' and the two sides of ↔ exchanged; regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le (|α τ| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for orthonormal τ) is the inequality of (P4), from which (d) follows by the orientation field; rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg is (P5); dtc_isIntegerMultiplicity_sub is part (c) under the extra hypothesis 0 < n (the case n = 0 is still covered by the argument above, which does not use n ≥ 1).
proof_key_steps: (d): Cauchy–Binet gives Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = 1 for orthonormal τ, so |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
(a): the density of Hⁿ⌞(M′∖M) vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6 on an exhaustion of U), so the blow-up integrals of M and M′ have the same limits.
(b): all IMRep fields restrict; the orientation field transfers by (a); continuity of the restricted current from local integrability and (d).
(c): on the overlap the approximate tangent spaces agree a.e., so the orientations differ by a sign; combine multiplicities θ_A ∓ θ_B, drop cancellation points, and verify the IMRep fields with (a).

subproblems.title: Restricting the domain preserves integer multiplicity (reused accepted dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and V ⊆ U ⊆ ℝ^P with V open. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity, i.e. T = τ(M, θ, ξ) for some IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of U (Simon 6.3.1). Then the restriction T⌞V ∈ 𝒟_n(V) is integer multiplicity in V. Here T⌞V = T.restrictDomain, T⌞V(ω) = T(ιω) with ι = testFormOnInclusion. Explicitly, T⌞V is represented by (M ∩ V, θ, ξ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity (T.restrictDomain hVU)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.restrict_im-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 8f3bacb2e7f68423e88b488e5939a0d419c646fb). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. Role in the parent proof: It is the last sentence of (F5) in the parent proof, an integer multiplicity current in ℝ^P regarded as a current in U_i. The parent uses it to make Y_i|U_i integer multiplicity, so that S_i + Y_i is integer multiplicity and has a weight (steps 7–8). The sibling retraction_comparison uses it for (π_#Y)|U. Its accepted proof cites its own accepted sibling (A) = dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.approx_tangent_local-a1, status accepted), which is contained in the same accepted candidate commit. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: step 5 of the parent proof (T' = T restricted to U' is integer multiplicity), with Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753) and Ch. 3, 1.4. Uses the sibling dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff, called (A) below.
Let R = (M, θ, ξ) = (R.carrier, R.mult, R.orient) be an IMRep of U with R.Represents T. Define R' with carrier M ∩ V, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. We check the fields of IMRep V n, then the representation.
1. Measurability: M is Borel and V is open, so M ∩ V is Borel.
2. M ∩ V ⊆ V.
3. Rectifiability: M ∩ V ⊆ M, and M is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
4. θ is measurable, and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M ∩ V ⊆ M.
5. Local integrability in V. Let K be compact with K ⊆ V. Then (M ∩ V) ∩ K = M ∩ K because K ⊆ V. Also K ⊆ V ⊆ U, so ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the local integrability of R in U.
6. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V), because Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono; AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
7. Orientation. By the field orients of R, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. A property holding Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. also holds Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), and Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ V (ae_restrict_mem; M ∩ V is measurable). Fix such an x. Then x ∈ V, M ∩ V ⊆ M, V is open, and (M ∖ (M ∩ V)) ∩ V = ∅ has Hⁿ-measure 0. So (A) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q, and the same Q still satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Hence R' is an IMRep of V.
8. Representation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). The form ιω has the same underlying form, so (T⌞V)(ω) = T(ιω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x). For x ∈ M ∖ (M ∩ V) we have x ∉ V ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and the integrand θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) vanishes (ξ(x) is linear). M is measurable and M ∩ V ⊆ M, so ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero), and the right side is R'.action ω. Thus R' represents T⌞V, and T⌞V is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict a representation (M, θ, ξ) of T to (M ∩ V, θ, ξ). Measurability, rectifiability, positivity and local integrability on compact subsets of V ⊆ U are inherited.
The orientation condition transfers: at x ∈ V, removing M ∖ V (which misses the open set V) does not change the approximate tangent plane (sibling A).
Forms supported in V vanish on M ∖ V, so the integral over M equals the integral over M ∩ V.

subproblems.title: Support of a current vanishing off a compact set (reused accepted rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

The sibling retraction_comparison uses it for spt Q ⊆ B̄_G ∩ spt S and spt(Z − S) ⊆ π(spt Y), and the sibling pushforward for spt π_#Y ⊆ π(spt Y). Source: parent proof, step 6(f) (“For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B̄_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K … S − T vanishes on all forms supported in B_{s/2}(y), whose closure is compact and contained in U, so y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ K. Being relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K ⊆ U, spt(S − T) is compact”), isolated for an arbitrary current F; the parent applies it to F = S − T.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.
